title: Bearings and Triangle Applications
short: Solve navigation and surveying problems with the laws of sines and cosines.
trouble: Students measure a bearing from the x-axis instead of from north.

blocks.html: Ships, planes and surveyors rarely meet right triangles. With the law of sines (handling the ambiguous case when it comes up) and the law of cosines, you can solve any triangle. Navigation adds one more idea: directions measured from north.

A bearing is measured clockwise from north, from $0^\circ$ to $360^\circ$. It can also be written in compass form such as N $40^\circ$ E: face north, turn $40^\circ$ toward the east. The standard-position angle (counterclockwise from east) is $90^\circ - \text{bearing}$, adjusted by $360^\circ$. To solve: use the law of cosines for two sides and the angle between them (SAS) or three sides (SSS), and the law of sines when you know an angle and the side across from it.

Navigators use north because a compass needle points there, and they turn clockwise because that is how compass dials are marked. Math class uses east and counterclockwise. Both describe the same directions; north is $90^\circ$ in standard position, and turning clockwise subtracts.

blocks.name: pre-bearing

opts.task: Set a course of S $30^\circ$ W. What bearing is that?

blocks.cap: Gold: the bearing, clockwise from north. Blue dashed: the same direction as a standard-position angle.

blocks.title: Converting directions
blocks.q: Write N $35^\circ$ W as a bearing and as a standard-position angle.
steps: Face north and turn $35^\circ$ toward the west. Clockwise from north that is $360^\circ - 35^\circ = 325^\circ$.
Standard angle: $90^\circ - 325^\circ = -235^\circ$, and adding $360^\circ$ gives $125^\circ$ (up and to the left, as expected).

blocks.title: Two hikers (law of cosines)
blocks.q: Two hikers leave camp. One walks $3$ km on a bearing of $20^\circ$; the other walks $8$ km on a bearing of $80^\circ$. How far apart are they?
steps: The angle between their paths at camp is $80^\circ - 20^\circ = 60^\circ$.

blocks.title: Across a river (law of sines)
blocks.q: Points $A$ and $B$ are $100$ m apart on one bank. A tree $C$ is across the river with $\angle A = 45^\circ$ and $\angle B = 105^\circ$. Find $BC$.

blocks.html: Measuring a bearing from the $x$-axis. A bearing of $40^\circ$ is not $40^\circ$ in standard position; it is $50^\circ$, because it starts at north. Sketch a compass rose with N at the top before you draw any triangle.
